subject: Proposal from architect
body: Architect analysis for #2474 Parts A/E/F. Parts B/C/D shipped in PR #2556. Remaining work decomposes into a 3-slice DAG per decision-1: slice-1 (Part E — promote ScriptedProvider to shared/egg_harness/testing/, add 8 k3s regression tests under integration_tests/regression/), slice-2 (Part A — add 'integration:' job to test.yml as sibling of unit/security so Test/aggregate remains the canonical required-check name per decision-2 and is required-from-day-1 per decision-3), slice-3 (Part F — generic CLAUDE.md + docs/guides/testing.md updates per Q6). slice-1 and slice-2 are siblings (no edge); slice-3 has one dep edge from slice-1 because Part F's docs reference the regression subdir slice-1 creates. Analysis names: key design choices (ScriptedProvider location, workflow_call placement, E.6 3-slice mid-PROPOSE scenario, E.7 minute-granular timing via consensus_timeout_minutes_plan=1, E.8 kubectl-logs scrape of gateway audit_log since there is no /api/v1/audit endpoint, E.3 coder-pushes-docs-file 403, generic Part F docs); 8 risks for risk_analyst (notably R5 scope-expansion cross-role coordination and R7 slice-2 .github/ role-eligibility verification — task_planner's commit 7f6de0f1b already shows this risk realized via .github-staging/ approach); seed acceptance criteria for task_planner. Architect did not touch any non-allowed paths.

subject: Proposal from risk_analyst
body: Risk assessment for #2474 plan phase. Identified 11 technical risks across CI reliability, scope, test implementability, compatibility, and security. Overall risk: MEDIUM; recommendation: PROCEED_WITH_MITIGATIONS. Top risks: R1 (HIGH) Required-from-day-1 gating concentrates flake risk on day one with 8 brand-new k3s scenarios — operator accepted but a flake-fallback posture should be pre-committed; R2 (HIGH) test.yml `aggregate` job's needs[] and result-conditional must be extended to include the new `integration` sibling job or the gate silently reports false success on integration failures; R3 (HIGH) operator's scope-expansion rule (failing-against-main tests trigger production-code fixes in slice-1 PR) opens unbounded scope on slice-1 — task-planner should reserve conditional task slots and the plan must include a HITL escape valve for substantial fixes. Medium risks: R4 ScriptedProvider promotion + 5 in-tree call sites; R5 E.8 push-counting has no gateway HTTP endpoint (recommend log-scraping over a new endpoint); R6 'Test / aggregate' check name silently coupled to workflow `name:` field. Low: R7-R11 covering test brittleness, slice-3 merge-order coupling, wall-clock budget, pytest auto-collection, and E.7 timeout tolerance. Three human-review areas registered, rollback plan documents per-slice revertibility, recommendations include flake-guard primitives (image-import retry, kubectl event capture) for slice-2.
